answer.decision: Use staged canaries with automatic abort thresholds and backward-compatible schema changes, but condition promotion beyond the 1% canary on an operational safeguard that can contain database-related errors within five minutes.
answer.action: Start a representative 1% canary, monitor error rate and p95 latency automatically for at least 12 minutes, and immediately disable the routing feature flag on a routing regression. Automatically initiate application rollback for a database-access regression. Promote through progressively larger stages only after healthy observation gates, targeting full traffic within one business day. Before exceeding 1% exposure, verify that traffic isolation or another tested containment mechanism can keep customer errors from exceeding 1% while the nine-minute application rollback completes; if no such mechanism exists, do not promote because the stated error-duration constraint cannot be guaranteed.
reasons: Staged canaries minimize initial exposure while providing useful production latency evidence.
Historical routing regressions appeared within four minutes, making automated error-rate and p95-latency gates appropriate.
The additive schema permits rollback to the old application without a schema downgrade.
The routing feature flag enables rapid containment of routing defects without redeployment.

A nine-minute application rollback is longer than the permitted five-minute duration for error rates above 1%, so automatic rollback alone is insufficient for database-related failures at broader exposure.
A global deployment creates avoidable risk, while production-identical staging would take six weeks and still omit third-party latency variance.
assumptions: The 1% canary is representative across regions, customer segments, and critical request types.
A complete failure confined to exactly 1% of traffic would not make the aggregate customer error rate exceed 1%.
Health thresholds and measurement windows are validated to detect meaningful regressions without excessive false aborts.
Healthy staged promotion can complete within one business day.
Any containment safeguard required before broader promotion will be tested and shown to act within five minutes.
risks: No stated mechanism contains database read-pattern failures within five minutes; without one, promotion beyond the initial canary may violate a hard constraint.
A 12-minute canary may miss delayed, low-frequency, regional, or segment-specific failures.
Aggregate metrics may conceal severe harm concentrated in a small region or customer group.
Automatic thresholds can either abort healthy stages or miss regressions outside error rate and p95 latency.
Failures may emerge only at higher load after early stages pass.

citations.claim: The previous three routing regressions were detectable through error rate or p95 latency within four minutes.
The additive schema remains compatible with the old application version, avoiding schema downgrade during rollback.
A 1% canary needs about 12 minutes to produce statistically useful latency signals.
Global application rollback takes nine minutes.
Production-identical staging would take six weeks and still omit third-party latency variance.
The routing path can be disabled by feature flag, whereas database read-pattern changes require application rollback.
The policy must prevent customer error rate from exceeding 1% for more than five minutes, avoid schema downgrade, and reach full traffic within one business day when healthy.
